title: Building separation to the adjoining property boundary at least the Table 2.7 distance (MR2, HR1, HR2, HR3)
text: A 2.7.1 Development complies with the separation requirements set out in Table 2.7.

replaces.note: Volume 2: up to 4 storeys refer 2.4 and 3.5; 5 to 8 storeys 9 m; 9+ storeys 12 m (all codes). Draft (MR2, HR only): 5+ storeys 9 m to R60 or below, 6 m to R80 or above

notes: Up to 4 storeys: refer 2.4 (Table 2.1) and 3.5 (Table 3.5), NOT_APPLICABLE here. Proposed fact adjoining.r_code (coding of the adjoining property on the boundary faced). Gaps (C4P2-075): no adjoining-boundary row for R80, LR1, R100, R160 or MR1, whose 5th storey and above rest on the 4 m side/rear setback, A2.4.2 and Table 3.5, but Table 3.5 fifth storey and above says 'Refer Table 2.7' (circular); 'coded' is undefined for uncoded adjoining land; R160 loses Volume 2's 9 m from the 5th storey. Net against R60 or below: 9 m unchanged at 5 to 8 storeys, 12 m to 9 m at 9+. Table 3.5A lists separation against 'A2.6.1' (C4P2-007).

verified.note: Table 2.7 (p22) adjoining rows apply to 'MR2, HR1, HR2 and HR3' only; the up-to-4-storeys cell is one merged 'Refer 2.4 Side and rear setbacks (Table 2.1) and 3.5 Visual privacy (Table 3.5)' across both rows; 'coded R60 or below / R80 or above' does not place uncoded adjoining land or R100-SL.
